gaps.sentence: She has ___ great progress since she changed schools.
gaps.explanation: make progress is the collocation; after 'has' the past participle 'made' is needed.

gaps.sentence: Over five hundred athletes will ___ part in the games.
gaps.explanation: take part in something means to participate in it.

gaps.sentence: We ___ breakfast on the terrace every morning in summer.
gaps.explanation: have breakfast/lunch/dinner is the standard collocation for eating meals.

gaps.sentence: The crash left several passengers seriously ___.
gaps.explanation: seriously injured is the standard collocation describing bad injuries in accidents.

gaps.sentence: The committee will ___ a decision next week.
gaps.explanation: make a decision is the fixed collocation; we do not 'do' or 'give' a decision.

gaps.sentence: He always ___ the truth, however unpleasant it is.
gaps.explanation: tell the truth is the fixed collocation; 'say the truth' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a speech at the wedding that moved everyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Make a speech' is the collocation; say/tell take different structures.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a fortune selling software online.
gaps.explanation: make a fortune means to earn a very large amount of money.
